Multimodal summarization with multimodal output (MSMO) has garnered more and more attention from researchers. Unlike unimodal output (e.g., text-only summary), MSMO aims at extracting the most salient information from different modalities and generating multimodal summaries, with a text summary and the most relevant images.

multimodal summary (text summary and selected images)
The paper generates multimodal summaries consisting of a text summary and selected relevant images.

Before conducting the human annotation, we set guidelines for the annotators, which include the above evaluation attributes, as well as the instructions to avoid cognitive biases...
After having 1,562 multimodal summarization examples, we ask three annotators to evaluate the quality of the multimodal summaries.
guideline: Before conducting the human annotation, we set guidelines for the annotators, which include the above evaluation attributes, as well as the instructions to avoid cognitive biases ...

Guidelines include evaluation attributes (text relevance, coherence, consistency, fluency; image quality; text‑image relevance; overall quality) and instructions to avoid anchoring, lead, and text bias.

The annotators evaluate the following aspects: • Text Summary-Relevance: how well the summary captures the most relevant and salient information... • Text Summary-Coherence: how well the summary is organized with sentences logically connected... • Text Summary-Consistency: how factual and faithful the summary is to the source document... • Text Summary-Fluency: how fluent each sentence in the summary... • Summary Images: how well the selected summary images represent the content... • Text Summary-Summary Images Relevance: how well the summary text and summary images match... • Overall Quality: the overall quality of the generated multimodal summary.
